vectors.title: a child may introduce a caveat its parent does not declare
vectors.why: Absence is ⊤, so introducing a constraint is narrowing, never widening.

vectors.title: settle is ordered by authority granted, not by magnitude
vectors.why: Escrow grants less freedom than immediate settlement, so it sits lower. An implementation that orders these by name or by enum index the other way round lets a child escape escrow.

vectors.title: a lower step-up threshold is narrower, not wider
vectors.why: A smaller `over` means more spends need a human. Numerically inverted, ordered correctly.

vectors.title: effect narrows toward read and never widens
vectors.why: Structurally identical to settle: most authority first, index is the lattice position.

vectors.title: genuinely incomparable rates are rejected rather than guessed
vectors.why: 100/PT10M permits fewer per burst than 500/PT1H but 600/hour sustained. Neither is narrower, so the comparator refuses instead of picking one.

vectors.title: meet takes the lower bound on every dimension
vectors.why: The fold is what re-applies ancestor constraints; it must never widen.

vectors.title: the meet of two different pinned discrete values is ⊥, not either operand
vectors.why: Returning either operand makes `meet` non-commutative, which is exactly what the property tests caught. ⊥ is a valid lattice element and deliberately not a valid wire value, so a fold that reaches it fails validation.

vectors.title: an unregistered caveat key fails validation
vectors.why: Fail closed on anything the registry does not define.
